titulo: What El Niño means for your winter
receta: el acusado equivocado + regla con matiz (adaptado de 016-el-nino-clima)
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que sigue el clima a su amigo que ya 'sabe' cómo va a ser todo el invierno, para decirle que mire el pronóstico local
regla_guardable: El Niño = odds, not a promise. Check your town's forecast at weather.gov.
fuentes: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion, October 8, 2026: El Niño Advisory, +2.1 °C in Niño-3.4, strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027
NOAA Climate.gov / CPC: El Niño tends to shift the jet stream and storm track; U.S. winter impacts are tendencies, not guarantees

frases.texto: Your winter forecast is being written thousands of miles from your house.
It's El Niño, and it's back.
Right now, the central Pacific along the equator is about four degrees Fahrenheit warmer than normal.
NOAA says a strong El Niño is likely to last through the winter, into March.
That warm water tends to shift the storm track.
So the South usually ends up wetter, and the northern states usually end up warmer.
Heads up: that's the odds, not a promise. Your town can still get a blizzard.
Before you plan around it, check your local forecast at weather dot gov.
Send this to the friend who already predicted the whole winter.
